stories.title: Flintshire village clears final hurdle to adopt Welsh name Pentre Moch
stories.summary: Northop Hall has been granted permission to formally adopt its historic welsh name – Pentre Moch. Flintshire County Council has formally approved the official use of Pentre Moch – which translates as ‘Pig Holding’ or ‘Pig Village’ – as the primary Welsh name for the village. stories.title: Flintshire Council rejects two-storey glamping pod plan at Cilcain
stories.summary: Flintshire County Council has refused a bid to turn two glamping pods into two-storey buildings at a farm in Cilcain, in the Clwydian Range Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. stories.title: Five candidates confirmed for Higher Kinnerton by-election
stories.summary: A by-election will be held in Higher Kinnerton on Thursday 15 October to elect a new Flintshire County Council county councillor. The vote follows the resignation of Mike Allport, who held the seat as an Independent. Five candidates have been confirmed as validly nominated by returning officer Neal Cockerton.
